name: ChatGPT
description: Explore ideas, practise prompting, and turn public practice material into drafts and explanations.
openness: Hosted assistant. Using ChatGPT does not give you downloadable model weights or make inference local.
useful_for: A useful starting exercise is iterative writing: give a clear goal, ask for a draft, then request a specific revision. Web features also support research and creating files; availability depends on your account.
exercise: Ask for a 150-word invitation to a fictional community science night. Request a plain-English revision and check that it has not invented a venue or date.
limits: Confident wording is not evidence. Verify facts, calculations and citations. A browser conversation is not the same workflow as a terminal agent with access to a project.
considerations: Review account privacy, saved context and connected tools before use. Do not connect government storage or grant broad permissions just to complete a learning exercise. These are practical risk checks, not a comprehensive controversy review.

name: Claude
description: Practise drafting, explaining code and iterating on small visual or written artefacts.
openness: Hosted Anthropic assistant. Claude in the browser is distinct from the Claude Code harness on your laptop.
useful_for: Try revising a public passage for a different audience or creating a simple webpage with Artifacts. Inspect the result rather than assuming a polished artefact is correct.
exercise: Ask for a one-page fictional community garden FAQ. Ask which statements require evidence, then check or remove them.
limits: Generated text and code need review. Features and usage limits vary by plan. A preview of a webpage does not prove its accessibility, security or correctness.
considerations: The product offers integrations and connected knowledge. In this programme, do not connect work email, government accounts or internal MCP servers. Check the service's current privacy terms; no finding that it is controversy-free is made here.

name: Gemini
description: Explore Google's assistant with public text and fictional examples, keeping accounts separate.
openness: Hosted Google assistant. Gemini the service is not interchangeable with a downloadable open-weight model.
useful_for: Try explaining a public concept at different levels of detail and comparing how the same prompt works across assistants.
exercise: Ask for an explanation of a solar eclipse for a ten-year-old and for an adult beginner. Verify both against a public science source.
limits: Responses can be inaccurate. Connected apps and account settings change what context the assistant can use; keep government accounts and services disconnected.
considerations: Google's Gemini privacy notice describes activity use for service improvement and human review, with behaviour depending on settings. Deleting activity does not necessarily delete material already reviewed. Inspect the Privacy Hub before using any upload or screen-sharing feature.

name: Grok
description: Compare another assistant's explanations and its handling of uncertainty and evidence.
openness: Hosted xAI chat. The website is separate from the Grok terminal tool and its model configuration.
useful_for: Use the same public question as in another assistant, then compare factual support, uncertainty and tone—not just fluency.
exercise: Ask it to explain the difference between a comet and an asteroid, list uncertainties and identify sources you can check.
limits: A conversational style or current-looking answer is not proof of accuracy. Do not treat social posts or generated images as verified evidence.
considerations: Documented controversy: on 12 January 2026, Ofcom opened an investigation into X concerning Grok-generated sexualised imagery. That announcement is not a final finding against the standalone Grok website; this profile does not establish the investigation's present outcome. Do not generate intimate images, impersonations or harmful material.

name: Microsoft Copilot
description: Explore the public assistant—not GitHub Copilot CLI or your government's Microsoft 365 environment.
openness: Hosted Microsoft consumer assistant. Similar product names do not imply the same account boundary or data protections.
useful_for: Practise brainstorming and checking a short explanatory answer. Learn to identify exactly which Copilot product and account you are using.
exercise: Request a checklist for a fictional neighbourhood book swap. Check for unnecessary collection of personal information.
limits: Outputs can contain mistakes. Do not assume consumer Copilot has the same terms or protections as an agency-approved work service.
considerations: Microsoft publishes separate privacy guidance for individual and work/school experiences. Check the signed-in account and permissions before typing. Use only a dedicated learning account; do not sign into an organisational workspace.

name: Perplexity
description: Explore search-led answers and practise checking the sources behind a summary.
openness: Hosted search-and-answer interface. An interface can offer multiple models without itself being an open model.
useful_for: Find starting points for a public topic and practise following citations back to their original context. Search features and model choices depend on the account.
exercise: Ask how rainbows form. Open two cited sources and check whether each actually supports the attached claim.
limits: Citations make checking possible; they do not guarantee that a summary is accurate, complete or fairly represents a source.
considerations: Documented dispute: Cloudflare reported in August 2025 that Perplexity-associated crawling bypassed website preferences. This is Cloudflare's attributed technical account, not a court finding. We could not inspect Perplexity's linked response during this review, so this is not a resolved or complete account. Discuss source consent and attribution as well as answer quality.

name: Mistral Vibe Chat
description: Mistral's hosted assistant, formerly Le Chat. Explore another route from conversation to a reviewed draft.
openness: A hosted service from a provider that also releases model weights. A provider's open releases do not make every product open-source or local.
useful_for: Try drafting a short public guide and asking follow-up questions. Compare a chat workflow with the separate coding-agent workflow.
exercise: Draft a fictional walking-club welcome note. Ask for a shorter version and check that accessibility claims are not invented.
limits: Availability of agent features, connectors and usage limits varies by plan. Verify answers and permissions before taking actions.
considerations: Distinguish claims about enterprise self-hosting or data residency from the terms of the public chat website. Do not connect government tools. Check the licence of any specific model release separately; a brand name is not a licence or approval.

name: Qwen Chat
description: Explore a hosted assistant from the Qwen team and learn how chat services differ from released model weights.
openness: Qwen releases include open-weight models. For example, Qwen3-0.6B has an Apache 2.0 licence. This dated example is not a claim about every Qwen release or the model currently serving Qwen Chat.
useful_for: Compare explanations or simple coding suggestions across model families. Use the release documentation to practise reading a model card and licence.
exercise: Ask for pseudocode to sort a fictional book list. Separately read the Qwen3-0.6B model licence and identify what it does—and does not—tell you about hosted chat privacy.
limits: Hosted chat sends input to a service; it is not local inference. Benchmark claims do not demonstrate reliability on your exercise or performance on an old laptop.
considerations: Evaluate the operator, processing location, retention, content filtering and account terms before use, as for every provider. This review verified the release example, not Qwen Chat's data residency or agency approval. Do not infer privacy from open weights.
sources: Qwen team: Qwen3 release and chat link, 29 April 2025

name: Hugging Face Models
description: Explore model cards and licences—not a vetted software store. Start with reading, not downloads or demos.
openness: A hub contains releases with different licences and levels of openness. Being listed does not certify a model as open-source, safe or suitable.
useful_for: Learn to identify the publisher, intended task, licence, limitations and hardware requirements before selecting a model.
exercise: Without downloading or running anything, inspect a model card and file list. Record the publisher, exact revision, licence, file formats, custom-code requirements and scan warnings. Mark anything unknown. Explain why a clean scan or a safetensors file alone cannot approve the whole workflow.
limits: Model cards, benchmark tables and popularity are not independent assurance. Downloads may be large, and an old laptop may not have enough memory. A repository's licence, code, model behaviour and hosting arrangements each need separate checks.
considerations: Treat community repositories and demos as untrusted until reviewed. Hugging Face provides security checks, but its documentation explicitly warns that scanning is not foolproof and custom model code can be malicious. Being hosted on the Hub is not government approval. Start by reading model cards; ask your facilitator before downloading weights, running commands or entering data into a demo.
sources: Hugging Face: loading and custom model precautions
Hugging Face: pickle risks and scanner limitations
Hugging Face: model cards and licence metadata

risk_checks.title: Loading can execute code
risk_checks.body: Some model files use Python pickle, which can execute code when loaded. trust_remote_code=True permits repository-supplied model code to run. Do not enable it or run copied install/notebook commands just to make an example work. A reviewed, pinned revision limits unexpected changes; it does not make malicious code safe.
source: Hugging Face: loading and custom model precautions

risk_checks.title: A scan badge is not a safety certificate
risk_checks.body: An unflagged file may still be unsafe. Prefer safetensors where supported to avoid pickle's code-loading mechanism, but that does not validate surrounding scripts, dependencies, model behaviour or data rights. Stop at a warning or an unclear file format and ask for review.
source: Hugging Face: pickle risks and scanner limitations

risk_checks.title: Spaces are other people's applications
risk_checks.body: A Space can be a community-built app with outbound network access. Treat prompts and uploads as information supplied to its operator, potentially forwarded to another service. Check who runs it and where information goes. Never paste API tokens into an unfamiliar demo, and never send OFFICIAL or non-public material.

risk_checks.title: Open access is not permission or suitability
risk_checks.body: Check the exact model's licence, provenance, intended use and limitations. Do not infer lawful training data, unbiased outputs or acceptable safeguards from a model card or download count. Device/product restrictions still apply to models obtained through a mirror or third-party host. Missing information is a reason to pause, not guess.
source: Hugging Face: model cards and licence metadata

name: DeepSeek
description: Learn about an open-weight model family and why technical openness does not override government restrictions.
openness: DeepSeek-R1 is a dated open-weight example with MIT-licensed code and weights; distilled variants also have base-model licence considerations. This is not a blanket claim about every DeepSeek release.
useful_for: An educational case study in separating model capabilities, release licences, hosting privacy and device-use policy. No service launch or model download is offered here.
exercise: Using the policy summary and source references below, explain why public inputs and a separate network do not by themselves authorise use of a restricted product.
limits: Do not access, install or run DeepSeek on government systems or devices contrary to applicable directions. Moving a model to a different host or running it locally is not an assumed exception.
considerations: Australian PSPF Direction 001-2025 requires government entities to prevent DeepSeek use/installation on government systems and devices. A repurposed learning laptop may still be in scope even off-network. The deployment owner must establish applicable requirements and any authorised exception. Separately, DeepSeek's February 2026 privacy policy says service personal data is processed and stored in the People's Republic of China. The hosted-service policy is distinct from model licensing.
sources: DeepSeek: R1 release and licence notes (reference, not an installation task)
